newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Italy told to use EU funds or lose them.
newsitem.headline: Italy told to use EU funds or lose them.

text.p: The European Commission told the Italian government on Monday to speed up the use of EU funds allocated to the country's less developed regions or risk losing them.
At the end of last year, Italy had only spent 14.3 percent of the amount put at its disposal by the Commission for the period 1994 to 1999, a Commission spokeswoman told reporters.
This meant payments worth some 1.6 billion European currency units ($3.14 billion) to railways, telecommunications and other infrastructure projects were behind schedule.

EU Regional Affairs Commissioner Monika Wulf-Mathies warned Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi at a meeting in Brussels that some regions, namely Campania in the South, may be in danger of losing the funds altogether if the projects were not speeded up, the spokeswoman said.
At the end of 1996, Campania had only used 0.7 percent of the total 2.89 billion Ecus it was agreed for the six-year period.
There was no sugestion of fraud but rather of bad management and deficient administrative structures as well as a lack of training and equipment to carry out the projects.
The situation was particularly worrying regarding money pencilled in for farm and social projects, the spokeswoman said.
Ciampi committed Italy to doing better in the future, pledging to spend 38 percent of the total money by the end of the current year -- an objective acceptable the Commission.
